questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to grow chilli peppers at home in pots
Why spices can be bad for your health
Pepper: its history, types and effect on food
The life of a famous French chef in Paris
questions.why: They discuss pepper, including its history, different varieties, colours and effect on flavour.

questions.q: What surprising fact does Neil share about peppers?
options: They are the fruit of very tall climbing vines
They grow underground, just like potatoes
They only grow in the south of France
They were first used as a medicine in China
questions.why: Neil says peppers are the fruit of vines often growing over ten metres high.

questions.q: How was pepper viewed in the past, according to Becca?
options: It was only used by poor people in the countryside
It was thought to be dangerous to eat
It was mainly used to preserve meat in winter
It was highly valued; explorers sailed for it
questions.why: She says pepper was prized as 'the black gold of ingredients' and explorers crossed oceans for it.

questions.q: What was unusual about Mathilde Roellinger as a young girl in Paris?
options: She cooked in her father's restaurant after school
She put pepper, not sugar, on her yoghurt
She refused to eat any spices at all
She grew pepper plants in her garden
questions.why: While other girls sprinkled sugar on yoghurt, Mathilde was sprinkling pepper.

questions.q: According to Mathilde, what does pepper do to food?
options: It hides the taste of the other ingredients
It makes food less spicy
It makes other flavours stronger without hiding them
It makes food last longer
questions.why: She says it will not disguise the other ingredients but 'push them': it's a flavour catalyst.

questions.q: What does the colour of pepper depend on, according to John Laurenson?
options: How ripe the peppercorns are and how they're treated
The country where the pepper plant grows
The variety of pepper plant that is used
The amount of rain the plant gets each year
questions.why: He says colours don't correspond to varieties but to the maturity of the peppercorns and processing.

questions.q: What colour are peppercorns when they are mature and dried?
options: Green
Red
Grey
Black
questions.why: He says they're green when young, black when mature and dried, red when very mature.

questions.q: What is Mathilde's opinion of grey pepper?
options: It's her favourite kind
She doesn't like it, calling it 'grey dust'
She thinks it's the most natural pepper
She uses it in all her cooking
questions.why: Grey pepper is an industrial creation; Mathilde calls it grey dust and isn't keen on it.
